blocks.title: Lattice energy
blocks.text: The lattice energy of an ionic crystal, delta Hlatt, is the enthalpy change when one mole of the ionic compound is formed from gaseous ions under standard conditions: Na+(g) + Cl-(g) gives NaCl(s), delta Hlatt = -787 kJ per mol.

The lattice energy depends on the charge on the ions and the size of the ions. Lattice energy decreases as the size of the cation or anion increases, because the packing of oppositely charged ions becomes less tight; the lattice energies of the alkali metal halides fall from LiF towards CsI. Lattice energy is directly proportional to the charges on the ions. Lithium fluoride and magnesium oxide have the same arrangement of ions and ions of comparable size, but MgO has delta Hlatt = -3923 kJ per mol against -1049 for LiF: the doubly charged Mg2+ and O2- ions attract each other much more strongly than the singly charged ions of the same size. For ions of similar size, the greater the charge the higher the charge density and the stronger the ionic bonds.

blocks.text: Solubility trends of group 2 hydroxides and sulfates

Delta Hsol depends on both the lattice energy and the hydration enthalpy. Down group 2 both hydration energy and lattice enthalpy decrease, because the charge density of the cations falls. For the hydroxides the lattice energy decreases more rapidly through Mg(OH)2, Ca(OH)2, Sr(OH)2 and Ba(OH)2 than the hydration energy of Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+ and Ba2+, so the lattice energy dominates, delta Hsol becomes more exothermic and the solubility increases. For the sulfates the sulfate ion is much larger than hydroxide, so the decrease in lattice energy from MgSO4 to BaSO4 is less, while the hydration energy of the cation falls by a greater amount; hydration now dominates, delta Hsol becomes more endothermic and the solubility decreases from MgSO4 to BaSO4.
